misconceptions.description: Believing a personal site is improved by adding more pages and sections rather than by matching pages to a single audience and purpose
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes blog, gallery, guestbook, and other pages a hiring-manager audience did not need
misconceptions.feedback: Start from one audience and one goal. Keep only the pages that help that reader reach the evidence they came for. Extra pages dilute the path, they do not strengthen it.

misconceptions.description: Using vague labels like Stuff, Things, or Click Here instead of descriptive labels that let a visitor predict the content
misconceptions.trigger: learner names a section with a non-orienting word
misconceptions.feedback: Rename the label so a scanning reader can predict what is behind it. A good label answers What will I find here before the click.

misconceptions.description: Adopting an AI-generated sitemap wholesale even when it was built for a business rather than a single-author student portfolio
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps AI-suggested pages such as Pricing or Careers that do not fit the actual purpose
misconceptions.feedback: Treat the AI sitemap as a proposal. Judge each page against your audience and purpose, keep what fits, and write down why you cut the rest.
